title: Year four close: the house of many rooms
hookLine: the Catechism, Aquinas, the orders, justice, Mary and the East: rooms in one house
tomorrow: Year five opens: reading for yourself

cards: A supper table at night, and friends who have just heard their teacher say he is going away. In John's Gospel, Jesus tells them not to let their hearts be troubled, and gives them a picture of a house.

In the Douay-Rheims: "In my Father's house there are many mansions." Mansions here means dwelling places, rooms to live in, and the next words speak of a place prepared for them. It's a promise about heaven.
It's also a fair picture of this year: a walk through one house, door after door, each room lived in. Today, the year four close.

teach.h: THE CATECHISM IS THE FLOOR PLAN.
teach.b: On day five hundred eighteen, this verse gave you the line a place for you. Walk back through the house.
The first room was the Catechism, read part by part: what Catholics believe, how they celebrate, how they live, and how they pray. That's the floor plan; every other room sits on it.
Next, a study, with Thomas Aquinas at the desk, asking a question, listing the objections fairly, answering with patience.

teach.h: A STUDY, AND A HALLWAY OF ORDERS.
teach.b: Then a long hallway of religious orders. Benedictines, with their rule of prayer and work. Franciscans, with poverty and joy.
Dominicans, preaching truth. Jesuits, finding God in all things. Carmelites, climbing into silent prayer.
Different rooms for the same Gospel. Then the room that opens onto the street: Catholic social teaching, the dignity of every person, the common good, a preference for the poor.
A quieter room with Mary: her feasts, her titles, what the Church teaches about her.
A door some Catholics in the West rarely open, into the Eastern Catholic churches, with their own liturgies and icons, in full communion with Rome.

And the devotions, the callings and the neighbors: the rosary on a kitchen table, the vocation of a married couple or a hermit, a greeting sent to Muslim, Jewish and Hindu friends. Yesterday, Catholics disagree.

teach.h: IN MY FATHER'S HOUSE THERE ARE MANY MANSIONS.
teach.b: Today, where they disagree: inside one house. A Benedictine and a Jesuit pray in different rooms, under one roof, at one table. Not a hotel of strangers.
A family home, with doors open between the rooms.

how: Catholics live their faith through different schools of prayer and thought within one Church: some are drawn to a religious order's spirituality, some to social justice, some to Marian devotion or the Eastern liturgies, all sharing the same creed and sacraments.

o: the year's last lesson, with nothing more to learn
a walk back through the year's rooms in one house
a final test on everything the year has taught

games.q: the rooms of year four — tap the pairs.
p: dwelling places in the Father's house

s: in John's Gospel, the line about many mansions is spoken at supper
Jesus speaks it at supper with his friends, as he tells them he is going away.
in this line, mansions means grand estates
it means dwelling places, rooms to live in.
the religious orders are rival churches
they are different rooms for the same Gospel, under one roof, at one table.

games.q: you've walked through every room of the year. which one should you live in most?
o: the one you think you should like.
the one where you already feel most at home.
games.why: the practice asks you to choose the room that's already yours, then do one small thing to live in it.

practice: Walk back through the year: the Catechism, Aquinas's study, the orders, social justice, Mary, the East, the devotions and the callings.

Notice which door you keep coming back to, not the room you think you should like but the one that's already yours, and picture one small way to live in it. If you pray, you can thank God for that room.

wordCard.voice: Year four close. A year of schools of prayer and thought, walked like the rooms of one house, from the Catechism to the neighbors at the door. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: many dwelling places, in John 14:2, rendered many mansions in the Douay-Rheims.

carryVoice: Your line: a house with many rooms. Every room is still there to come back to. Year five opens tomorrow.

sources.q: In my Father's house there are many mansions.
